fledgling.title: Fledgling
fledgling.author: Octavia E. Butler
fledgling.why: Comments are mostly negative about the book.

wind in the willows.title: The Wind in the Willows
wind in the willows.author: Kenneth Grahame
wind in the willows.why: Gentle riverbank adventures of Mole, Rat, Badger and Toad; a cosy children's classic with warm humour.

titus groan.title: Titus Groan
titus groan.author: Mervyn Peake
titus groan.why: First Gormenghast novel, set in a vast decaying castle with grotesque characters; rich, gothic and unlike other fantasy.

choice.title: The Choice
choice.author: Edith Eger
choice.why: A Holocaust survivor and psychologist tells her story of survival and healing; readers find it powerful and uplifting.

marabou stork nightmares.title: Marabou Stork Nightmares
marabou stork nightmares.author: Irvine Welsh
marabou stork nightmares.why: A comatose Scottish man replays his violent past while imagining a hunt in Africa; harsh, dialect-heavy Welsh.

girls.title: The Girls
girls.author: Emma Cline
girls.why: Comments are mostly unrelated or negative.

post office.title: Post office
post office.author: Charles Bukowski
post office.why: Bukowski's semi-autobiographical tale of a drunken, wisecracking postal worker; darkly funny and fast.

paladin of souls.title: Paladin of Souls
paladin of souls.author: Lois McMaster Bujold
paladin of souls.why: A grieving dowager sets out on a pilgrimage and finds a mystery; a Hugo-winning, warm and thoughtful fantasy.

empire of silence.title: Empire of silence
empire of silence.author: Christopher Ruocchio
empire of silence.why: A far-future space opera told by a fallen hero recalling his youth; readers praise its scale and prose.

unworthy.title: The Unworthy
unworthy.author: agustina bazterrica
unworthy.why: Bazterrica's follow-up to Tender Is the Flesh, a bleak dystopia in a walled city; liked, though many prefer her first.

homage to catalonia.title: Homage to Catalonia
homage to catalonia.author: George Orwell
homage to catalonia.why: Orwell's first-hand account of fighting in the Spanish Civil War; compelling and less famous than his novels.

english patient.title: The English Patient
english patient.author: Michael Ondaatje
english patient.why: Four damaged people shelter in an Italian villa at the end of World War II; lyrical and slow-burning.

cathedral.title: Cathedral
cathedral.author: Raymond Carver
cathedral.why: Spare, powerful short stories of ordinary people; the title story is often named among the best ever.

molokai.title: Moloka'i
molokai.author: Alan Brennert
molokai.why: A girl sent to Hawaii's leper colony grows up there; immersive, well paced and moving.

plainsong.title: Plainsong
plainsong.author: Kent Haruf
plainsong.why: Quiet, touching stories of people in a small Colorado town; praised for plain, beautiful prose.

between two kingdoms.title: Between Two Kingdoms
between two kingdoms.author: Suleika Jaouad
between two kingdoms.why: A young writer's account of cancer and recovery; readers say it is fantastic and read it fast.

northanger abbey.title: Northanger Abbey
northanger abbey.author: Jane Austen
northanger abbey.why: Austen's playful satire of Gothic novels, following a girl who imagines horrors at an old abbey.

dawn of everything.title: The Dawn of Everything
dawn of everything.author: David Graeber and David Wengrow
dawn of everything.why: Challenges the standard story of early human society with new evidence; readers say it changed how they see history.

needful things.title: Needful Things
needful things.author: Stephen King
needful things.why: A mysterious shop sets neighbours against each other in a Maine town; readers say it kept them engaged throughout.

exodus.title: Exodus
exodus.author: Leon Uris
exodus.why: Sweeping novel of the founding of Israel after World War II; a school favourite that readers loved.

antidote.title: The Antidote
antidote.author: Karen Russell
antidote.why: Dust Bowl Nebraska and a woman who stores others' memories; slow, beautifully written and a book-club hit.

wrong place wrong time.title: Wrong Place Wrong Time
wrong place wrong time.author: Gillian McAllister
wrong place wrong time.why: A mother keeps reliving the day her son commits a murder; an inventive time-twisting thriller.

fablehaven.title: Fablehaven
fablehaven.author: Brandon Mull
fablehaven.why: Two siblings discover a magical creature preserve; a popular children's fantasy series starter.

ninefox gambit.title: Ninefox Gambit
ninefox gambit.author: Yoon Ha Lee
ninefox gambit.why: A soldier teams with the ghost of a traitor general in a calendar-based space war; dense but inventive.

ballad of songbirds and snakes.title: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes
ballad of songbirds and snakes.author: Suzanne Collins
ballad of songbirds and snakes.why: Prequel to The Hunger Games following the young future President Snow; fans of the series enjoy the backstory.

mountains sing.title: The Mountains Sing
mountains sing.author: Nguyen Phan Que Mai
mountains sing.why: A Vietnamese grandmother and granddaughter live through war across generations; readers find it moving.

alive.title: Alive: The Story of the Andes Survivors
alive.author: Piers Paul Read
alive.why: True account of the rugby team who survived a plane crash in the Andes; absolutely gripping.

foreigner.title: Foreigner
foreigner.author: C. J. Cherryh
foreigner.why: A human interpreter among aliens navigates politics and tea-drinking diplomacy; praised for superb alien worldbuilding.

go tell it on the mountain.title: Go Tell It on the Mountain
go tell it on the mountain.author: James Baldwin
go tell it on the mountain.why: Baldwin's semi-autobiographical novel of a Harlem boy and his family's religious life; moving and rich in flashbacks.

bloom.title: Bloom
bloom.author: Kevin Panetta
bloom.why: Title matches different books; comments name another author.

pisces.title: The pisces
pisces.author: Melissa Broder
pisces.why: Comments are split and mostly negative.

always coming home.title: Always Coming Home
always coming home.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
always coming home.why: Le Guin's experimental anthropology of a future people, mixing stories, poems and maps; a favourite of devoted readers.

hangsaman.title: Hangsaman
hangsaman.author: Shirley Jackson
hangsaman.why: A shy college girl slips into unreality in a haunting, psychological Shirley Jackson novel loved by her fans.

compound.title: The Compound
compound.author: Aisling Rawle
compound.why: Young women compete on a reality-TV style compound; a sharp, unsettling debut that readers devoured.

steel beach.title: Steel beach
steel beach.author: John Varley
steel beach.why: A lunar reporter's life gets weird in Varley's witty future world; many readers call it a favourite of his.

shockwave rider.title: The Shockwave Rider
shockwave rider.author: John Brunner
shockwave rider.why: Brunner's 1975 tale of a hacker on the run in a networked society, eerily close to the present.

witch king.title: Witch King
witch king.author: Martha Wells
witch king.why: A demon king wakes after years and untangles a political plot; praised though the cast and names take effort.

jonathan strange mr norrell.title: Jonathan Strange and Mr. Norrell
jonathan strange mr norrell.author: Susanna Clarke
jonathan strange mr norrell.why: Two magicians revive English magic during the Napoleonic wars in a witty, footnoted alternate history.

doppelganger.title: Doppelganger: A Trip into the Mirror World
doppelganger.author: Naomi Klein
doppelganger.why: Klein explores how a mistaken identity illuminates conspiracy culture and today's politics; readers say it makes sense of the moment.

source.title: The Source
source.author: James A. Michener
source.why: Michener's huge saga of one archaeological dig in Israel and the layers of history beneath it; a good thick read.

prince.title: The Prince
prince.author: Niccolo Machiavelli
prince.why: Machiavelli's guide on holding political power, famed for its cold realism; some find it dry.

ask the dust.title: Ask the dust
ask the dust.author: John Fante
ask the dust.why: A young writer's poverty and doomed love in 1930s Los Angeles; a raw, confessional voice.

ella minnow pea.title: Ella Minnow Pea
ella minnow pea.author: Mark Dunn
ella minnow pea.why: Letters vanish from an island's alphabet in this epistolary novel; a quirky, witty and fast read.

i am pilgrim.title: I am Pilgrim
i am pilgrim.author: Terry Hayes
i am pilgrim.why: A retired spy hunts a bioterrorist in a sprawling thriller; a long, fast and enjoyable page-turner.

daisy darker.title: Daisy Darker
daisy darker.author: Alice Feeney
daisy darker.why: A family gathers at an isolated house and begins dying; a twisty mystery readers call great.

cats eye.title: Cat's Eye
cats eye.author: Margaret Atwood
cats eye.why: An ageing painter revisits her childhood and a friend who bullied her; many name it their favourite Atwood.

skippy dies.title: Skippy Dies
skippy dies.author: Paul Murray
skippy dies.why: Boys at an Irish boarding school, comic and tragic; readers call it genius and read it quickly despite its length.

woman in the dunes.title: The Woman in the Dunes
woman in the dunes.author: Kōbō Abe
woman in the dunes.why: A man is trapped in a sand pit with a woman; surreal, allegorical and unsettling.

sourdough.title: Sourdough
sourdough.author: Robin Sloan
sourdough.why: A programmer takes up baking after a magical starter arrives; a quirky, light read.

best offer wins.title: Best Offer Wins
best offer wins.author: Marisa Kashino
best offer wins.why: A woman becomes obsessed with winning her perfect house in a cutthroat housing market; a gripping, fast thriller.

everyone in my family has killed someone.title: Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone
everyone in my family has killed someone.author: Benjamin Stevenson
everyone in my family has killed someone.why: A mystery at a family reunion, in the style of Agatha Christie; recommended especially on audio.

speak.title: Speak
speak.author: Laurie Halse Anderson
speak.why: A teenager goes silent after a traumatic event; a powerful, widely read school book that hit readers hard.

sailor who fell from grace with the sea.title: The Sailor Who Fell from Grace with the Sea
sailor who fell from grace with the sea.author: Yukio Mishima
sailor who fell from grace with the sea.why: A widow's lover and her son's cruel gang in postwar Japan; short, chilling and elegant.

miracle in the andes.title: Miracle in the Andes
miracle in the andes.author: Nando Parrado
miracle in the andes.why: A survivor of the Andes plane crash tells it first-hand; readers find it fantastic and moving.

undaunted courage.title: Undaunted Courage
undaunted courage.author: Stephen E. Ambrose
undaunted courage.why: Ambrose's account of the Lewis and Clark expedition; readers rate the storytelling, though some find it heavy going.

annie bot.title: Annie Bot
annie bot.author: Sierra Greer
annie bot.why: A lifelike robot companion begins asserting herself in her owner's home; a thought-provoking, quick read.

interpreter of maladies.title: Interpreter of Maladies
interpreter of maladies.author: Jhumpa Lahiri
interpreter of maladies.why: Quiet, perfectly written stories of Indian and Indian-American lives; a Pulitzer-winning collection readers love.

quincunx.title: The Quincunx
quincunx.author: Charles Palliser
quincunx.why: A young heir uncovers a tangled Victorian inheritance mystery; tightly plotted with twists readers did not see coming.

red dragon.title: Red Dragon
red dragon.author: Thomas Harris
red dragon.why: An FBI profiler hunts a serial killer with help from Hannibal Lecter; a gripping thriller.

gate of the feral gods.title: The Gate of the Feral Gods
gate of the feral gods.author: Matt Dinniman
gate of the feral gods.why: Fourth book in the Dungeon Crawler Carl series, a violent, funny LitRPG that fans devour.

stardust.title: Stardust
stardust.author: Neil Gaiman
stardust.why: Comments are lukewarm; praise is mainly for the film.

jazz.title: Jazz
jazz.author: Toni Morrison
jazz.why: Comments are lukewarm and mention struggling with it.

wizard of the crow.title: Wizard of the Crow
wizard of the crow.author: Ngugi wa Thiong'o
wizard of the crow.why: A magical-realist satire of a post-colonial African dictatorship; readers call it brilliant and funny.

startide rising.title: Startide Rising
startide rising.author: David Brin
startide rising.why: A dolphin-crewed starship is stranded on a hostile planet in a space opera focused on adventure.

mad mabel.title: Mad Mabel
mad mabel.author: Sally Hepworth
mad mabel.why: An elderly woman secretly kills people she thinks deserve it; funny, poignant and a bit disturbing.

decameron.title: The Decameron
decameron.author: Giovanni Boccaccio
decameron.why: A hundred tales told by young people sheltering from the plague, ranging from comic to tragic; a Renaissance classic.
